title: One day in Busan: follow the east coast

slides.title: Stay on the east coast
slides.voice: Only one day in Busan? Keep to the east coast, so you spend minutes—not hours—getting between stops.

slides.title: Start at a seaside temple
slides.sub: Go early, before it gets busy
slides.voice: Start at Haedong Yonggungsa, a temple on the rocks above the sea. Go early, and keep your voice low at this place of worship.

slides.title: Beach, then market snacks
slides.voice: Head back to Haeundae Beach for a walk, then find lunch in the streets behind it. The nearby traditional market is good for snacks like fish cakes and tteokbokki.

slides.title: Ride the coastal line
slides.sub: Book sky capsules ahead on busy days
slides.voice: If you have time, the Blueline Park beach train and sky capsules follow the coast from Mipo to Cheongsapo. Sky capsule tickets can sell out at busy times.
slides.photo_query: Haeundae Blueline Park sky capsule Busan

slides.title: Dinner by the sea
slides.sub: See Gwangan Bridge lit after dark
slides.voice: Return to Haeundae for dinner, then walk the beach at night or take a short taxi ride to Gwangalli Beach for views of the lit-up bridge.
